newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Small-cap interest underpin Singapore noon shares.
newsitem.headline: Small-cap interest underpin Singapore noon shares.

text.p: Keen interest on small issues continued to underpin Singapore stocks at midday on Thursday, dealers said.
"There is some interest from both retail clients and institutional buyers who are looking for bargains in the market. But the buying was still focussed mainly on smaller-cap stocks," a dealer said.
He said market sentiment was still neutral with the benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index hovering above the psychological 2,000 level.
At midday, the index was down 8.75 to 2,015.11. Market voulme was moderately active with over 72.9 million shares traded. Losers led gainers by 160 to 101.
Focus was still very much on infrastructure-based Van der Horst which topped the actives with over 10 million shares changing hands. It ended up 22 cents at S$2.70.

Malaysian issues traded over the counter were weak on talk of some U.S. houses calling for a sell on bank stocks on expectations of weak earnings.
